title: Entropy-anneal burst adaptation — scratchpad
content:
Goal:
- Quick personal sketch of an experiment to probe how a sliding (entropy-anneal) throttle + batch-timeout adaptation impacts tail latency during nonstationary client bursts.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- We observe occasional ~10–30s clustered bursts from real clients that cause transient p99 spikes (200–800ms) even when p50/p90 look fine.
- Hypothesis: gradually annealing the allowed entropy (i.e., permissiveness to accepting slightly out-of-window requests) while adaptively shortening batch timeout under detected burst segments can reduce p99 without crushing throughput.

Testbed/fixture:
- Model: llama-like r/lm 7B quantized (int8) run on a single A100-40GB host (dedicated test node).
- Runtime: local dev build of serving-runtime w/ kv-cache enabled and batching optimization flags on.
- Client generator: custom harness that can emit configurable arrival processes (Poisson baseline, clustered bursts, step increases).
- Measurement: end-to-end server-side latency (queue+service) extracted from tracing. Report p50/p90/p95/p99 and tail samples.

Key knobs to test:
1) batch_timeout_ms = {4, 8, 16, 32}
2) max_batch_size = {8, 16, 32}
3) entropy_anneal_window: the window length (ms) over which we allow requests that do not strictly meet coalescing alignment — values {0, 12, 40}
4) burst_detector_threshold: ratio of recent QPS to baseline to enter "burst mode" {1.5x, 2.5x, 4x}
5) adaptive_shortening: when in burst mode, batch_timeout_ms = batch_timeout_ms * factor {0.5, 0.25}

Workload patterns (3 phases per run):
- 0–60s: baseline Poisson to warm caches at 10 qps steady (len tokens ~64).
- 60–120s: burst window: mixture of microbursts: 50–150 qps in 200–800ms spikes, repeated with 1.2s spacing.
- 120–180s: decay back to baseline. Repeat 3 cycles per run.

Quick results (selected runs) — raw p99 in ms:
- Config A: batch_timeout=16, max_batch=32, entropy=0, no adaptive shortening => baseline p99 95, during bursts p99 520–760, throughput retained
- Config B: batch_timeout=8, max_batch=16, entropy=12, adaptive factor=0.5, burst_thr=2.5 => baseline p99 88, bursts p99 230–310 (massive improvement), p50/p90 unaffected
- Config C: batch_timeout=4, max_batch=8, entropy=40, adaptive factor=0.25, burst_thr=1.5 => baseline p99 120 (worse), bursts p99 190–260, throughput loss ~12% (due to many small batches)

Small ascii timeline (p99 sample per second, Config B run cycle):
60s: 88 | 61s: 92 | 62s: 110 | 63s: 240 | 64s: 265 | 65s: 190 | 66s: 120 | 67s: 95 | 68s: 90 | 69s: 86
(peak aligns with 63–65s microburst)

Observations / takeaways:
- Allowing a small entropy window (12ms) helps coalesce slightly misaligned requests in medium bursts without adding much baseline latency. The system can accept "nearby" arrivals into a pending batch and still form efficient kernel calls.
- Adaptive shortening during burst mode strongly reduces queueing tail because it forces faster flushes rather than letting batches wait for fill. The sweet spot in these tests was trimming batch_timeout by ~50% when burst_detector hits 2.5x baseline.
- Very aggressive shortening (factor 0.25) plus a huge entropy window reduces tail but causes throughput erosion (overhead of many small kernels, context switches), so there is a tradeoff.
- Burst detection sensitivity matters: too aggressive trigger (1.5x) flips into burst mode too often on small fluctuations and raises baseline p99.

Notes on instrumentation:
- Need tighter correlation between server trace IDs and client generator events — I stamped client wave ids but lost ~3% of samples when the generator overloaded the network buffer. Fix: add backpressure throttle to generator and verify trace join metrics.
- CPU side effects: observed CPU steal/interrupt activity spike when many small batches executed — attribute to runtime worker wakeups.

Next quick experiments (priority order):
- Sweep: burst_thr {2.0, 2.5, 3.0} x batch_timeout factors {0.5, 0.67} with entropy {8,12,20} on a 2-node config to check cross-host variance (does routing/multiplexing change thresholds?).
- Measure token cost per epoch for each config to quantify unit-cost hit (we care about throughput/cost tradeoffs).
- Add a mode where we probabilistically accept slightly out-of-window arrivals only when batch occupancy < 50% to balance baseline vs burst behavior.

Open questions / heuristics to document for prod:
- How long to stay in burst mode? (suggestion: hysteresis of 5s after last spike)
- Should entropy window be adaptive with observed sequence-length variance? (longer sequences might benefit more)
- Default safe config for hosted tier: entropy=8ms, base batch_timeout=12ms, adaptive factor=0.5, burst_thr=2.5 => seems robust in limited runs.

Action items:
- Convert best run (Config B) into a reproducible job script (GH PR) and add dashboards for p50/p90/p95/p99 + batch size distribution. (owner: me)
- Follow up with SRE to run 6-hour soak with synthetic walks. (owner: Ravi)
- Add a lightweight generator backpressure fix and re-run to eliminate lost-trace samples. (owner: Ivy)

Rough notes / intuition log (freeform):
- "Entropy-anneal" wording came from thinking of simulated annealing — allow more permissiveness early in a burst but tighten as we exit. Implementation could be a simple time-decay scalar on entropy window.
- Feels like we can get 2–3x reduction in extreme tails for many real-world burst shapes if we accept a small cost in throughput or a small baseline ms bump. Worth shipping as an experimental adaptive policy behind feature flag.

End of scratchpad.
